name: Scheduled-task liveness census - pair every task to an output oracle
description: Blueprint 95 of 96 (design BP-MNT-04). Pair every scheduled task with an OUTPUT-FRESHNESS oracle, so a task that reads GREEN while producing nothing for weeks becomes visible. Mechanism: task state and output freshness are two INDEPENDENT signals and only their PAIRING is informative - neither alone is a verdict. Two decoding rules keep it from generating false alarms: a non-zero last-result code is not automatically a failure (a single-instance refusal is a designed steady state), and machine power-off windows are subtracted before an output is called stale. A task with NO oracle is a gap to fix, not a pass.

task_source.description: Where the task list comes from. Named explicitly because a census over the wrong scheduler silently returns a healthy empty set.

output_oracles.description: Per task: the artifact it should be producing, how often, and what counts as fresh (mtime, a growing byte count, a new row). A task absent from this list is reported NO-ORACLE.

designed_nonzero_results.description: Task names whose non-zero last-result code is their DESIGNED steady state - e.g. a single-instance supervisor refusing a second launch. These must be classified EXPECTED-REFUSAL, never FAILING.

power_off_windows.description: Intervals the machine was off. Subtracted from output age before staleness is judged; without this the census raises a false alarm after every weekend.

max_concurrency.description: Tasks paired in parallel; the work is I/O-bound metadata reads

task-enumerator.description: Enumerates tasks from the declared scheduler and decodes each last-result code without assuming non-zero means failure

freshness-oracle.description: Measures output freshness against the expected cadence, with power-off windows subtracted. Never reads task state - that is the other signal.

pairing-adjudicator.description: Joins the two independent signals into one verdict, and is required to report NO-ORACLE rather than infer health from task state alone

routes.reason: the pairing is the whole idea; the two measurements feeding it are mechanical

signals-are-independent.expression: state_read_by_enumerator == true AND freshness_read_by_oracle == true AND oracle_read_task_state == false

stages.title: Enumerate tasks and DECODE each last-result code

work_unit.title: Enumerate every scheduled task and decode its state and last-result code
work_unit.question_or_target: Enumerate tasks from the declared scheduler and record, per task: enabled state, last run time, and the last-result code with its DECODED meaning. Do not assume non-zero means failure - check the code against designed_nonzero_results first and record which rule applied.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: decoding a result code against a designed-refusal list is the step that stops this census generating false failures

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per task the raw state fields as the scheduler reported them plus the decoded meaning and the rule that produced it; a decoded verdict with no raw code cannot be re-checked
tests_required: a task listed in designed_nonzero_results with a non-zero code must decode to EXPECTED-REFUSAL, not FAILING
a task with a non-zero code NOT on that list must decode to FAILING
both-states control: the same decoder must produce different verdicts for those two inputs - a decoder that returns one answer for both is not decoding
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the pairing adjudicator reads only the raw plus decoded fields, never the enumerator's summary of task health
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9501 emitted only when every task carries its raw state and a decoded result with the rule named; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9501 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: one retry if the scheduler API is unavailable; a second failure means the census is INCOMPLETE and must say so explicitly rather than reporting the tasks it managed to read as the whole set

stages.title: A designed refusal is not a failure
Output freshness, with power-off windows subtracted

work_unit.title: Measure one task's output freshness against its expected cadence
work_unit.question_or_target: Measure the declared freshness signal for one task's output and compute its age with the declared power_off_windows subtracted. Compare against expected_cadence_seconds. Do NOT read the task's state - that is the other signal and reading it here would collapse two signals into one.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: mechanical measurement; the judgement is in the pairing stage

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the freshness signal read, its raw value, the raw age, the subtracted power-off seconds, and the adjusted age against the cadence
tests_required: a stale output whose staleness is entirely explained by a power-off window must NOT be reported stale
an output that does not exist at all must be reported ABSENT, distinct from stale - an absent artifact and an old one are different findings
no task-state field may appear in this artifact - the signals must stay separable
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: none for the measurement; the pairing adjudicator is the reviewer of its meaning
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9502 emitted only when raw age, subtracted window and adjusted age are all recorded for this task; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9502 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - a filesystem metadata read that fails twice is an access problem, and the honest output is ABSENT with the reason

stages.title: The pairing is the verdict - neither signal alone is one

work_unit.title: Join task state with output freshness and classify every task
work_unit.question_or_target: Join the two artifacts and classify each task: HEALTHY (state fine AND output fresh), GREEN-BUT-DEAD (state fine AND output stale or absent), EXPECTED-REFUSAL (designed non-zero result), FAILING (undesigned non-zero result), NO-ORACLE (no output declared - unmonitorable by construction). Flag NO-ORACLE tasks as a gap to fix, never as a pass.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: cross-examining: it exists to refuse the single-signal verdict either measurement would license on its own

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per task both signals with their sources and the joined verdict; plus the NO-ORACLE count as a standalone field, because that number is the real finding of a first run
tests_required: a task whose state reads fine and whose output is 19 days stale must be GREEN-BUT-DEAD, not HEALTHY
a task with no declared oracle must be NO-ORACLE and must not be counted in the healthy total
both-states control: a task that is genuinely healthy must be classified HEALTHY - a classifier that never returns HEALTHY is alarming, not measuring
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader who re-derives two verdicts from the two source artifacts without reading this one
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9503 emitted only when every enumerated task carries one of the five verdicts and the NO-ORACLE count is a standalone field; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9503 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - the join is deterministic over two artifacts on disk

stages.title: A task with no oracle is a gap, not a pass

estimate.measurement_source: 09-WORKFLOW-BLUEPRINT-LIBRARY.md#BP-MNT-04 failure class 6 - a scheduled task read GREEN while its feed was dead for weeks (the recall-index case), and a supervisor task whose non-zero result code is its designed single-instance refusal

impact.blast_radius: read-only over scheduler metadata and output mtimes; writes only under command-center/census/**. It never enables, disables or triggers a task.

derived_from.credit: owner - stall detection from mtimes alone is impossible; the only honest mtime signal is 'wrote recently', so a verdict needs a second signal

rollback_to: reading the scheduler's own task list with no oracle pairing

x_extensions.mechanism: two INDEPENDENT signals per task - declarative scheduler state and output freshness - measured by different roles that are forbidden from reading each other's field, then joined into a five-way verdict. Two false-alarm suppressors are first-class: designed non-zero results and power-off window subtraction. NO-ORACLE is its own verdict because an unmonitorable task is a gap, not a pass.

not_a_duplicate_because.vs_firing-path-revalidation: that TRIGGERS a path and looks for a side effect, then compares against its own previous scorecard. This one cannot trigger anything - a scheduled task's cadence IS the subject - so it pairs a declarative state with an artifact's age instead. Trigger-and-observe vs state-times-freshness.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_detector-truncation-audit: that compares two counts of one population; this pairs two different KINDS of signal about one task. Both are two-signal designs and neither is a rename of the other.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_the_dead-feed-recovery_workflow: a recovery workflow REPAIRS one dead feed reactively; this is a periodic census whose most valuable output on a first run is the count of tasks that have no oracle at all.

contraindications: NOT for one-shot tasks - they have no cadence to be stale against
NOT for tasks with no observable output - fix that first, and this census names them so it can be fixed

benchmark_cases.given: the supervisor task whose non-zero code is a single-instance refusal
a task whose state reads fine and whose output is 19 days old with no power-off window to explain it
a daily task whose output is 60 hours old across a 48-hour power-off window
benchmark_cases.expect: HEALTHY - the adjusted age is 12 hours

worked_examples.terminal_state: SUCCESS:BPW-9503 with escalation - 1 GREEN-BUT-DEAD, 1 NO-ORACLE, 1 EXPECTED-REFUSAL correctly not counted as failing
worked_examples.note: Three of the four rows would be misread by a single-signal reading. State alone calls all four Ready-and-successful tasks healthy; freshness alone calls the supervisor's frequent writes healthy while flagging the reaper mid-run. Only the pairing separates them - and the fourth row exists only because the census refuses to omit a task it cannot monitor.

unverified: The NO-ORACLE count on this estate is UNVERIFIED and is the real finding of a first run - no number here is measured. Settling experiment = run the census and count tasks with no declared oracle.

Power-off windows are supplied as a PARAM rather than measured from the system event log. That keeps the workflow replayable (no clock, no event-log dependency) but means a wrong window silently changes a staleness verdict. Settling experiment = cross-check one declared window against System event IDs 6005/6006 and confirm the adjusted age matches.
